title: DHgate Sellers Are Scammers ?
body:
Warning: DHgate sent me the wrong item, then sided with the seller despite clear evidence — buyer beware
I want to share my experience so other OzBargainers go in with eyes open before ordering from DHgate. I was stupid I didnt check the sellers credibility and trusted the DHgate platform.
What happened
I ordered a "15.6inch Full Viewing Angle IPS Electronic Album" — a 15.6" digital photo frame — for $85 (Order #320431148131). What arrived was a completely different item: a small 7-inch digital clock.
I opened a dispute and supplied everything DHgate asked for: photos of the package, photos of the item received, its size, its weight, and an unpacking video. The seller's response was to submit a photo of the correct product — which proves nothing, since a seller obviously has access to correct stock in their own warehouse and can photograph it any time, before or after the fact. There's no way to verify that photo was actually of the item dispatched to me.
How the dispute was handled
After weeks of back-and-forth with support staff giving vague, repetitive responses, DHgate closed the dispute in the seller's favour on 6 August 2026. Their stated reason: my evidence "did not include a valid unpacking video," while the seller's packing video and weight evidence were accepted as sufficient.
When I pushed back, DHgate's follow-up response was essentially: contact the seller yourself and try to negotiate a refund directly, and if the seller agrees, get them to put it in writing so DHgate can "look into options." As a goodwill gesture for being sent the wrong item and having my dispute rejected, I was offered a $5 coupon toward a future purchase.
Why I think this is a broader pattern, not a one-off
Since the dispute closed, I've noticed the seller's original listing has been taken down/edited, with the product description now matching a smaller item rather than the 15.6" version I ordered — even though my order history clearly shows I purchased the 15.6" listing. To me, that suggests a pattern of substituting cheaper stock for what's advertised, and relying on buyers not documenting every unboxing to get away with it.
Bottom line
DHgate's dispute process puts the burden of proof almost entirely on the buyer, while accepting easily-fabricated "evidence" (a photo of stock, taken who-knows-when) from the seller as sufficient.
Customer service responses were slow, repetitive, and offered no meaningful resolution beyond a token coupon.
I've effectively lost $85 with no real path to a refund unless the seller — who has already shown bad faith — voluntarily agrees to one.
If you're thinking about ordering from DHgate, especially higher-value items, know that if something goes wrong, the platform's dispute process may not have your back. I won't be using DHgate again.
Happy to answer questions if others have had similar experiences with this seller or platform.
I have reported this transaction to ACCC and my Financial Institution to whom I have paid.
